notices.html: Pick-your-own is over for the season at all six farms we track, and Thanksgiving has passed. Terhune's Winery Weekend Music Series has been running Saturdays and Sundays through November, but the month is ending, so call before you drive. Some farms sell Christmas trees and wreaths starting about now, call ahead to ask rather than assume.

Polar Express runs this very weekend, Nov 27 to 29, at both Whippany (Morristown & Erie) and Phillipsburg (Delaware River Railroad). If you don't already have a ticket, call about last-minute openings: the next 2026 dates are Dec 4 to 6, 11 to 13 and 18 to 20.

Princeton's Palmer Square tree lighting is traditionally the evening of the Friday after Thanksgiving (this year, Nov 27), with Santa switching on the lights around 5pm. We could not confirm the exact 2026 time, so check palmersquare.com or call before heading over.

blurbs.terhune: This weekend: still no apple picking for the 2026 season. The Winery Weekend Music Series has been running Saturdays and Sundays through November, noon to 5pm with live music 1 to 4pm, but call 609-924-2310 to check whether this is the last weekend before you drive over. Ask about Christmas trees and wreaths too, some years they start about now.
blurbs.leeturkey: This weekend: Thanksgiving is behind you, so the big turkey rush has passed and the farm stand should be back to normal hours. Call 609-448-0629 before driving over to check what's in stock.
blurbs.vonthun: This weekend: the fall festival and corn maze season has wrapped, leaving just the farm market. Hours tend to shrink heading into December, so call 732-329-8656 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.emerys: This weekend: berries are long done, and the corn maze and hayrides were only listed through late October, so that part of the season is over too. Call the picking hotline at 609-758-8514 or check emerysfarm.com before you go.
blurbs.battleview: This weekend: still no apple picking, the spring freeze wiped out the whole crop this year. The country store stays open 9am to 5pm daily except Tuesdays, with cider donuts made from sourced apples. Call 732-462-0756 to ask about Christmas trees too, some years they're sold starting about now.
blurbs.johnsons: This weekend: the Thanksgiving pie rush is over, and the weekend Harvest Festival and corn maze have typically wrapped by now. Johnson's has run holiday hayrides and sold Christmas trees in past seasons, so call 609-654-8643 or check johnsonsfarm.com to see what's on this year.
blurbs.diggerland: This weekend: Diggerfest ended Nov 15 and the park is in its winter break. Check the park's own calendar for any December special-event weekends before driving down.
blurbs.sixflags: This weekend, Holiday in the Park continues at Six Flags Great Adventure: four themed lands, a 65-foot tree, nightly tree lighting, Santa photos and s'mores fire pits, included with park admission and with Silver, Gold and Prestige passes. It runs select dates through Jan 3, and Thanksgiving weekend tends to be one of the busiest, so buy tickets online first. Check sixflags.com/greatadventure for the date calendar.
blurbs.morven: This weekend: Festival of Trees continues, decorated trees and mantels fill the historic house's galleries for the holidays through Jan 10. Included with regular admission, check morven.org for current hours.
blurbs.whalewatch: This weekend: humpback season off Belmar typically winds down by November, so a trip this late is unlikely to be running. Check with the operator before planning around this one, we couldn't confirm current status this week.
blurbs.buckstubing: This weekend: Delaware River tubing is a summer operation and is almost certainly closed for the season by now. Check rivercountry.net before planning a trip, it usually reopens in late spring.
blurbs.dinosafari: This weekend: the Freehold run's listed season looks like it wrapped in late October. Call ahead or check before planning a visit, we couldn't confirm if it's still open this far into fall.

events.title: Winter Chalet makers' market
events.desc: Four lit chalets beside the library plus about fifteen rotating weekend craft vendors, free to walk through, in a run that spans Thanksgiving weekend into December.
events.note: Vendors rotate most weekends; the exact season end date wasn't confirmed this week, call the Arts Council of Princeton if unsure

events.title: Holiday in the Park
events.desc: Four themed holiday lands, a 65-foot tree, nightly tree lighting, Santa photos and s'mores fire pits, running select dates through Jan 3.
events.note: Thanksgiving weekend is typically one of the busiest dates, buy tickets online first and check the park's own calendar that today is an operating day

events.title: Festival of Trees
events.desc: Decorated trees and mantels fill the historic house's galleries for the holidays, running through Jan 10.
events.note: Included with regular admission, check morven.org for current hours

events.title: Holiday hayride (unconfirmed for 2026)
events.desc: Last year's Saturday-after-Thanksgiving program offered a hayride past the farm and a donation wagon for a free ride; this year's program wasn't confirmed when we checked.
events.note: Call 609-737-3299 before driving over. Howell is closed Sundays and Mondays regardless

extraPlaces.name: Winter Chalet Market, Hinds Plaza
extraPlaces.blurb: Four lit wooden chalets on the plaza beside Princeton Public Library, plus around fifteen weekend booths selling jewellery, ceramics, candles, prints, woodwork and kids' clothes. The weekend vendors rotate every week, so it is worth more than one visit, and it is easy Christmas shopping within fifteen minutes. Free to walk through.
extraPlaces.meta: Hinds Plaza, 66 Witherspoon Street, Princeton. Thursday to Sunday noon to 6pm, running through Thanksgiving weekend into December. Walk to Nassau Street for dinner afterwards.
